stem.en: A high concentration of salt or sugar keeps a pickle from spoiling. Why does this stop bacteria and fungi from growing?

text.en: Salt and sugar enter the cells and burst them from inside.

feedback.en: Water moves here, not the salt. The cells lose water and do not burst.

text.en: Water leaves the cells by osmosis, so they cannot grow.

feedback.en: Yes. The solution outside has far more solute than the inside of the cell.

text.en: Salt and sugar block all the light that the cells need.

feedback.en: Bacteria and fungi in a jar do not depend on light.

text.en: Salt and sugar make the walls of these cells grow much thicker and harder.

feedback.en: Salt and sugar do not build walls. Water loss is the cause.

explanation.en: The solution around the cell has far more solute than the inside of the cell. Water moves out of the cell by osmosis, and a cell that has lost its water cannot grow.

hints.en: Which way does water move when there is more solute outside the cell?
